To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
Fmr1 knockout and knockout mice with a human FMRP transgene exhibit different social behaviors.
Fmr1 KO mice carrying a human YAC transgene that overexpresses FMRP showed fewer active social approaches to partners than Fmr1 KO or WT mice, indicating correction of a behavioral response.

Fmr1 knockout (Fmr1 KO) mice carrying an FMRP-expressing human transgene (KOYAC mice) show a reduction in the number of active approaches to standard C3H/HeJ partner mice compared to their wild-type littermates (WT) and Fmr1KO controls.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development of a mouse model of Fragile X syndrome that can be used to study the molecular basis of the behavioral abnormalities associated with this disease and to test potential therapeutic interventions.
the development and use of animal models of human disease and with the behavioral and neurobiological mechanisms that underlie normal behavior and the etiology of behavioral disorders.
the study of the behavioral and molecular consequences of the fragile X mutation in mice.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
FMRP is necessary and sufficient for the regulation of social approach behavior.
overexpression of human Fragile X mental retardation protein in a knockout mouse model of the disorder corrects some, but not all, of the social behavior abnormalities.

overexpression of human Fragile X mental retardation protein (FMRP) in Fmr1-deficient (Fmr1 knockout) mice corrects or overcorrects several behavioral responses, including hyperactivity, anxiety-related responses, and social behaviors.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the KOYAC mice show an overcorrection of hyperactivity and social behavior, but not anxiety-related behaviors.
overexpression of human fragile X mental retardaton 1 protein (FMRP) can correct the social behavior phenotype of Fmr1 knockout mouse.
the social interaction test is a sensitive measure of the effects of FMRP deficiency and restoration in the Fmr1KO mouse model of FXS.
The main takeaway from our work is that
Fmr1KO and KOYAC mice show a similar pattern of social behaviors.
Fmr1KO animals show a number of behavioral abnormalities that are corrected by the overexpression of the human FMR1 gene.
the KOYAC mouse model is a useful tool for studying the molecular basis of the FMRP-mediated correction of social behavior in FXS.
